note: How did you hear about us? — the answers onboarding offers, written down once. The web list (src/lib/auth/signupSource.ts) and the iOS list (Core/SignupSource.swift) are both tested against this file, and the check constraint in supabase/migrations/20260911090000_signup_source.sql accepts exactly these values. Order is the order they are shown in, and it is part of the spec: the two answers that name a person come first, because they are the ones worth the most and the ones people scroll past.

detailLengthNote: Counted in Unicode code points, which is what Postgres char_length() counts, so a string either app accepts is a string the column accepts. Swift's String.count counts grapheme clusters instead and would let a 121-code-point answer through to a constraint violation at the end of onboarding, so the Swift side counts unicodeScalars.
